assertion_independence_note: Round-trip state comparisons use independent pre-removal reads and positive controls, not a variable passed as the expected persisted state; receipt and input-field propagation checks at 75,129,141,172,216 are not counted as independent version/semantic oracles. The persistence, no-committed-write and exact version guards have independent snapshots or fixture literals.

assertion_review.failure_condition_and_regression: Reinstating ledger.write in registration changes the independently captured tracked bytes; the recorded negative control demonstrates this exact failure.
Registering the wrong identity makes the literal registered expectation fail.
Returning an entry without persisting it makes the subsequent member read differ; the expectation is a return value, so this alone does not independently validate its fields.
Skipping removal or selecting the permanent member changes the literal reaped identity.
Reporting a reap without deleting session-idle leaves an extra persisted member.
Skipping the hold creation or misclassifying it does not return opened.
Dropping or changing the persisted reason fails the fixture-literal expectation.
Routing any mutation back through a tracked writer changes the pre-operation byte snapshot.
Restoring automatic roster/hold commits changes the independently sampled git HEAD.
Not advancing the imported version exactly once gives a value other than fixture version 7 plus one.
Reading the aggregate after deleting crew.json loses persisted roster, holds or version compared with the prior nonempty read.
Dropping imported members or holds, or resetting import version to zero, fails the nonempty positive control and fixture version 7.
Removing store-backed reads loses the seeded positive-control tuple when the aggregate is removed.
Incrementing on a repeated hold check or failing the first increment differs from literal version 8.
Opening a duplicate hold changes unchanged to opened.
Omitting the close increment differs from literal version 9.
Wrong elapsed-time computation differs from the independent 90-second fixture interval.
Losing the resumption_fired field on closure differs from the requested True; this is propagation coverage, not an independent check that a scheduler fired.
Restoring a file hold writer changes tracked fixture bytes.
Reading file state rather than stored closed holds fails after aggregate deletion.
Returning a different harness fails the supplied fixture literal; persistence is separately checked by cross-project reads.
Keying members by id without project overwrites the first project and changes its independent earlier snapshot.
Changing hold identity derivation to include project makes the deliberate collision fixture produce different IDs; this checks fixture collision, not persistence by itself.
Keying holds without project causes the second project to replace the first reason.
Losing the second project hold reason differs from its fixture literal.

Reimporting a deliberately emptied roster from the stale checkout returns seeded members; version equality here uses the writer return and does not independently guard version increments (literal guards are at 96,119,127).
Resurrecting the roster after aggregate removal returns members instead of an empty list.
Applying a removal before refusing changes the earlier captured rows or version.
Accepting a stale collection replacement removes the newly registered another identity.
Replacing holds while refusing the stale write changes the captured historic hold rows.
Committing the DELETE or first duplicate INSERT before an IntegrityError changes rows or version after rollback.
Skipping retirement or returning a different identity changes the receipt; the member_id is caller-supplied and this is receipt propagation, while 217 separately asserts removal.
Restoring a file-only retirement leaves the store member present.
Retiring through the tracked ledger changes the independent byte snapshot.
Falling back to persisting a registration when the store raises leaves a registered member.
Falling back to ledger.write when the store raises changes the independent byte snapshot.
Dropping or miscopying unscoped payloads during schema migration fails the independently seeded SQLite payload literals.
Failing to persist the scoped append or reopening without project isolation loses the expected scoped payload.
Scoped appends that overwrite the unscoped member alter its independently seeded payload.

findings.text: blocking: load now returns the auxiliary store version, whereas _write_state at :2845 and :2851 checks the unchanged file version; after registration or a hold changes version 7 to 8 only in the store, the existing production load/write pair in reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py:1186 and :1231 refuses an aggregate-held run's integrated-gate update as stale, even after rereading, so the version domains and their callers must be reconciled before landing.

justifications.durability: tests/test_members_and_holds_live_in_the_store.py:73 reddens when registration calls ledger.write again and :98 reddens when reads revert to the aggregate, but no added test covers the existing load/write caller at reckon/crew/promotion_gate.py:1231.
justifications.evidence: tests/test_members_and_holds_live_in_the_store.py:63-106 measures the stated gate, and the recorded base reproduction, 58/70-pass suite logs and negative-control.log show both green operation and the intended red tracked-path assertion.
justifications.fit: reckon/ledger.py:2222 and reckon/run_store.py:344 follow the existing ownership and naming idioms, but returning an auxiliary version at ledger.py:2304 breaks the surrounding version-paired public API.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/ledger.py:2254 and reckon/run_store.py:436 implement store-only versioned mutations, but reckon/ledger.py:2304 exposes a different version to an existing file writer.
justifications.reuse: Capability searches for collection persistence, schema migration, retry and version-conflict handling found the existing owners in reckon/run_store.py and reckon/_store.py:446; the new methods extend RunStore and reuse its retry helper, LedgerError and _store.VersionConflict rather than cloning the file-envelope implementation.
justifications.scope_discipline: The six changed files in the two source commits are contained in the source prompt's eight declared paths, including docs/evidence/fragments/history-persists-as-detail-washes-out/members-and-holds-in-store-s23.html.
